messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm opening a short proposal thread: add a lightweight client-side circuit breaker to our SDKs (TS/Go/Py) to reduce retry storms during quota/backpressure events. sketch below.

julian: Short explainer?

maya: Idea in one line: SDK maintains a small local state per-route/model (open/closed/probing). If the SDK sees a burst of 429s or connection errors above threshold within a window, it opens the breaker for T ms and either fail-fast or route to a configured fallback model. SDK emits an 'x-client-circuit' header: open|closed|probe so server + console can attribute.

sam: We already expose capacity signals server-side. Won't this duplicate? also split-brain concerns across regions.

maya: Server signals are useful but reactive. Client breaker avoids repeated retries that amplify failures and creates noisy telemetry. The header is optional — server behavior unchanged if header missing.

nina: Telemetry/console note: need to separate "client_opened" vs "server_rejected" events. Proposed metric keys: client_breaker_opened, client_breaker_probed, client_breaker_closed. Add tag client_breaker=true on spans/events. Console tile should show rate and per-team impact.

julian: Compatibility concerns: header is additive (non-breaking). But changing SDK retry semantics is behavior change — could affect apps that rely on current retries. Need opt-in vs opt-out decision.

sam: My vote: opt-in by default for public SDKs, but opt-out for internal Redwood workloads initially so we can test. Also require a server-side kill-switch (console toggle).

maya: Proposed rollout plan: 1) implement in SDKs behind flag (clientCircuitBreaker.enabled = false by default) with telemetry on when enabled. 2) server accepts header and logs event. 3) Console: add toggle + tile and a kill-switch. 4) Canary: enable telemetry-only on 5% traffic for 2w, then internal opt-in, then public opt-in, then consider default-on after 90 days if no regressions.

nina: Telemetry sampling: sample 100% for client_breaker events during canary. Add regression evals (latency, error-rate, token-cost) tied to code change.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident notice — prior quota storm (2024-08-21) caused ~30% tail latency spike; link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2024-08-21 (referenced dataset).

sam: Edge cases: long-lived connections / SSE / streaming — breaker state must be scoped carefully (per-route+client-instance or per-request?). I think per-client-instance with TTL and ability to reset on successful probe.

julian: SDK impl details: simple leaky-bucket + consecutive-429 counter. On open: schedule a probe request after backoff; if probe succeeds, close and reset. Expose local events so host apps can choose fallback (e.g., swap to cheaper model). Provide hooks: onOpen, onProbe, onClose.

maya: Docs snippet (will go in migration guide):
```
// TS example
const client = new RedwoodClient({ clientCircuitBreaker: { enabled: true, windowMs: 30000, threshold: 5, openMs: 60000 } });
// header included automatically: x-client-circuit: open|closed|probe
```

julian: Tests: add unit tests for state transitions, e2e with server-side simulated 429 bursts, and an integration run that validates console metrics pipeline.

nina: Console UX: new tile + per-team toggle + historical timeline. Also add an alert when client_breaker_opened rate > X% of requests for 10m.

sam: Security/compat: header content should be minimal (open|closed|probe). No auth, no PII. Server must ignore malformed values.

maya: Action items: @julian + @sam implement TS + Go prototypes, @nina wire telemetry schema, I'll draft migration docs and rollout plan. We'll sync in 48h.

julian: ack. I'll add a feature flag gate in the console for kill-switch. :thumbsup:

sam: ack from infra side, will validate streaming case.

nina: will draft telemetry schema and dashboard mocks.

maya: thanks — short follow-ups during sync. :rocket:
